clauses.mechanism: performed_by_own_terms: termination of the Executive Order 12947 emergency and revocation of Executive Order 12947, effective by section 4 at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 10, 2019
clauses.reason: The lead terminates the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12947 of January 23, 1995, revokes that order as amended by Executive Order 13099, and then, to build on those steps and take additional steps under Executive Order 13224, orders what follows. Section 4 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 10, 2019, so the termination and revocation were executed on that date (the signing date, September 9, 2019, is the alternative reading). They are one-time acts that have nothing left to operate on, so the clause is terminated by performance on 2026-10-14, and no held instrument restores the revoked order. The ordering words that introduce sections 1 to 4 continue as part of those sections.

clauses.current_legal_basis: The order's own held text read with the bounded searches current-law:usc, current-law:ecfr and later-events:ofr_catalog (coverage notes read). The national emergency declared in Executive Order 13224 of September 23, 2001, for which this order takes additional steps and which it amends, was continued by the Presidential notice of September 11, 2026 (91 FR 58805, FR Doc. 2026-19053), which recites this order and states that the emergency must continue in effect beyond September 23, 2026; the annual notices of September 18, 2020, September 15, 2021, September 19, 2022, September 7, 2023, September 18, 2024 and September 8, 2025 (FR Docs. 2020-21059, 2021-20351, 2022-20582, 2023-19744, 2024-21722, 2025-17552) are also held. The notice that would have fallen between this order (September 9, 2019) and September 23, 2019 is not held; the 2020 notice presupposes that the emergency had been continued, because an emergency not continued ends by operation of section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act. An OFAC notice (91 FR 64223, FR Doc. 2026-20525, published 2026-10-07) records designations made on 2026-10-02 under section 1(a)(iii) of Executive Order 13224 'as amended by Executive Order 13886' and notes secondary-sanctions risk under section 1(b) of Executive Order 13224 as amended by Executive Order 13886; the held eCFR text of 31 CFR part 594 (amended through 2026-11-06) rests on the order. The U.S. Code search covers release point 119-121, current through 2026-10-09, and the eCFR/CFR search is a point-in-time search as of 2026-10-14; laws enacted between 2026-10-09 and 2026-10-14 are not reflected in the Code edition and none affecting this order is held. No held instrument revokes, supersedes or amends the clause.
clauses.reason: Section 1 restates section 1 of Executive Order 13224 and, in section 1(a), blocks all property and interests in property of the persons described in the paragraphs below that are or come within the United States or the possession or control of any United States person. research_rationale:
Executive Order 13886 of September 9, 2019 (84 FR 48041), Modernizing Sanctions To Combat Terrorism, has four sections. The held Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_13886.txt, 84 FR 48041, PDF pages 1-3) carries the heading, the date September 9, 2019 and FR Doc. 2019-19895. The lead terminates the national emergency declared in Executive Order 12947 and revokes that order (as amended by Executive Order 13099) and orders further steps under Executive Order 13224. Section 1 restates section 1 of Executive Order 13224 (blocking of listed persons and of persons determined under criteria, correspondent-account sanctions on foreign financial institutions, and the exception clause); section 2 changes a cross-reference in section 5 of that order; section 3 holds general provisions; section 4 makes the order effective at 12:01 a.m. eastern daylight time on September 10, 2019. The dossier's 19 clauses (with the machine-split paragraphs of section 1(a)(ii) and (iii)) cover the whole text and are accepted. The lead's termination of the Executive Order 12947 emergency and revocation of that order were performed when the order took effect on September 10, 2019, so the lead is terminated by performance; the other 18 clauses are operative. Executive Order 13224 as amended by this order was applied in OFAC designations on October 2, 2026, and the emergency was continued by the notice of September 11, 2026. A search of the held corpus for the number EO 13886 (27 files) finds the order, continuation notices, OFAC notices and rules, 31 CFR part 594 and a 2024 BIS rule; the only revoke-wording is the statement that this order revoked Executive Order 12947. None revokes, supersedes or amends this order. Executive Order 14294 (an unlocated actor in the dossier) is an order on regulatory criminal penalties and does not name it. The held text is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF; page images were not inspected.
